items.title: Git in 10 Minutes: Save Every Version of Your Work (Beginner Tutorial)
items.description:
Learn Git from zero in about 10 minutes: save every version of your work, see exactly what changed, and go back in time when something breaks. Every command is run for real on one tiny project: init, add, commit, diff, log, restore, revert, .gitignore and your first branch.

Chapters
0:00 The result
0:29 What Git actually does
0:59 Install and check
1:33 Tell Git who you are
2:05 Step 1: git init
2:46 Step 2: add and commit
3:43 Step 3: see what changed
4:11 Step 4: the history
4:49 Undo: get back a broken file
5:28 Go back to any version
5:58 Undo a bad commit
6:45 Ignore files with .gitignore
7:19 Bonus: try ideas on a branch
8:03 Common mistakes
8:34 Pro tip: commit small, commit often
8:50 Recap

Commands from the video (all run for real, git 2.43):
git --version
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email you@example.com
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git init
git status
git add budget.py
git commit -m "First version of budget"
git status --short
git diff
git log --oneline
git restore budget.py                      (throw away uncommitted changes)
git restore --source=HASH budget.py      (load an older version of the file)
git revert HEAD                            (undo the last commit with a new commit)
git switch -c savings                      (new branch)
git commit -am "Try a savings goal"        (add tracked files + commit)
git switch main
git merge savings

.gitignore used in the video:
notes.log
__pycache__/

budget.py (first version):
income = 3000
rent = 1200
food = 450

left = income - rent - food
print("Left this month:", left)

Install Git for free from the official site: git-scm.com
